findings.before: For [-2,5,-4,1] at t=[0,1,2,3], NPV is zero at both 0% and -50%, but the solver discarded the tangent zero at 0% and certified -50% as unique. [1,-2,1] was incorrectly no_root.

findings.before: With cap=0, admission incremented the f6 migration INT_MAX cutover hold and raised a PostgreSQL integer overflow instead of preserving the day hold.
findings.fix: Treat the cutover counter as a held local date independently of the configurable cap; normal admission resumes on the next local date.

findings.before: List/filter/batch legacy quality queries chose the latest GATE by ID while detail chose timestamp then ID. Historical/delayed insert ordering produced contradictory HEALTHY and UNASSESSABLE responses.
findings.fix: Use timestamp then ID consistently in effective quality-status queries.

findings.before: Excluding the last target marked a generated health round DONE even when its due date was thirty days later. Other linked treatment completion paths reject early completion.

findings.before: The first re-review of a revision-zero legacy decision overwrote the known original reviewer, timestamp and note; only the new decision entered history.
findings.fix: Forward f9 migration snapshots known legacy metadata as immutable revision zero, and the API lazily snapshots post-upgrade imported legacy decisions before overwriting the current projection. previous_status equals status for a baseline, avoiding an invented unknown earlier transition. Refuse downgrade that would destroy snapshots.
